topics.topic: Stable listing-to-read file identity and owning association
questions: Which module owns the stable association between a source id reported ready during the listing and the exact listed path that may later be read, so that `read_source_bytes` never searches for another file with the same content, including an ignored conflict copy?

What identity or handle must `observe_source_files` return and `read_source_bytes` accept so placement reads only the exact entry judged at listing time and never locates another file by source id or content?

quotes:
- `SourceFile`, what `source_folder` reports about one file to `photo_delivery`. It holds the server path
  of the file and never leaves the service; M02 is the form a caller sees;
- reading the bytes of one source file without following a link;

A name is judged as the directory listing returns it, and that judgement holds for the whole scan. R0-14 concerns files, not content: a conflict copy is
never a source of a new placement, an ordinary file with the same content as a conflict copy is placed
as usual, and content that already has a placement replays under A3 rule 2 whatever name it has now. A
file renamed after the listing is no longer at the listed path, so reading it for placing fails
with `unreadable_file` (A3 rule 4).
judgement.why: The texts make source_folder responsible for the read and pass photo_delivery a SourceFile containing the exact server path observed, while the rules require a failed read at that listed path rather than locating equal content elsewhere.

topics.topic: Module ownership of expanded INV-18 placement outcome and no-write guarantee
questions: Does `source_folder` own all of the expanded INV-18, including the placement outcome and guarantee that nothing is written, or does `photo_delivery` own that part?

quotes: | A1 | order 1 to 8, ignored names, walking order | `source_folder` |
| A1 | order 9 to 11, placed and published status | `photo_delivery` |
- ignored names, links, the settling time, source limits and file signatures;
- reading the bytes of one source file without following a link;
- whether a photo was placed or published;
- one placement per project and content, replay, and per-photo failure;
| `photo_delivery` | `source_folder` | `observe_source_files`, `read_source_bytes` |
judgement.why: P3 already judged the same INV-18 ownership and enforcement boundary, and the relevant State 3 unit is unchanged since closure.

precedent.topic: Ownership and enforcement boundary for INV-18 conflict-copy exclusion during placement
quotes: | A1 | order 1 to 8, ignored names, walking order | `source_folder` |
| A1 | order 9 to 11, placed and published status | `photo_delivery` |
- ignored names, links, the settling time, source limits and file signatures;
- reading the bytes of one source file without following a link;
- whether a photo was placed or published;
- one placement per project and content, replay, and per-photo failure;
| `photo_delivery` | `source_folder` | `observe_source_files`, `read_source_bytes` |
precedent.why: The texts assign conflict-name eligibility and safe source reading to source_folder, assign the placement decision to photo_delivery, and explicitly declare the two source_folder symbols that photo_delivery imports; source_folder can therefore own INV-18 by making conflict copies ineligible without owning placement records or placement status.

topics.topic: Module responsible for classifying a listed file that disappears before reading
questions: When a file reported by the placement scan disappears before `read_source_bytes`, which module decides that the item is `unreadable_file`: `source_folder`, which hides disappearance handling, or `photo_delivery`, which owns per-photo failure?

quotes: | A1 | order 1 to 8, ignored names, walking order | `source_folder` |
| 6 | opening or reading it fails, including a file that disappeared or became a link | `rejected` | `unreadable_file` |
- directory traversal and the handling of files that disappear during it;
- one placement per project and content, replay, and per-photo failure;
judgement.why: Source_folder owns and applies A1 rule 6 to classify the failed read as unreadable_file, while photo_delivery owns reporting that already-decided failure as the placement item's per-photo outcome.
